title: In-Context Multi-Operator Learning with DeepOSets
claim: An encoder that pools example input-output pairs into a permutation-invariant context feeds a decoder that predicts outputs at query points.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, encoder and decoder brackets over a unified dataflow
description: A left-to-right architecture diagram split into two labeled halves by brackets. The left half, "Deep Sets (Encoder)", takes context pairs (u_1, G(u_1)) through (u_n, G(u_n)) in gray. Each pair goes through a shared yellow φ block and produces blue embeddings h_1 through h_N. These feed a green Pooling block that outputs a pooled vector h. Small gray dotted-curve sketches below the encoder show u_i and G(u_i). The right half, "DeepONet (Decoder)", has a yellow Branch network that takes the query function u_q (in blue) and h. A yellow Trunk network takes the query location x_q. Each outputs coefficient nodes, b_1 to b_p and t_1 to t_p, shown as blue circles in boxes. A red multiply circle combines them to give the red output Ĝ(u_q)(x_q). The eye goes first to the yellow blocks and then to the red output.
caption: DeepOSets architecture for in-context multi-operator learning.
abstract: An important application of neural networks in scientific computing is non-linear operator learning. In this framework, a neural network is trained to fit a non-linear map between infinite dimensional spaces, for example, the solution operator of ordinary and partial differential equations. Recently, inspired by the discovery of in-context learning for large language models, an even more ambitious paradigm has been explored, called multi-operator learning. In this approach, a neural network is trained to learn many different operators at the same time. At inference time, the network is passed a small number of example input and output pairs to disambiguate the desired operator. In this work, we provide a precise mathematical formulation of the multi-operator learning problem, propose a parameter-efficient, attention-free architecture, called DeepOSets, and prove its universality in the in-context multi-operator learning task. We perform experiments demonstrating the efficacy of DeepOSets on several benchmarks, including Burgers' equation, 1D and 2D Darcy flow, and a variety of initial-value and boundary-value differential equations. In a comparison with the transformer-based ICON model on the 1D Darcy problem, under a small training budget (10k steps), DeepOSets attained lower error at every context size with 19% of the parameters, while with an extended budget (100k steps), ICON attains 26-41% lower error, but at the cost of roughly 218$\times$ more training time, 12$\times$ higher inference latency, and 5.3$\times$ more parameters.
